finding: NHANES 2021-23 has 15 strata x 2 PSUs (df = 15); every cohort row has WTPH2YR > 0; jackknife SE agrees with Taylor linearisation (ratio within 2%).
decision: WTPH2YR for all cohort analyses and the weighted ablation; WTSAF2YR for fasting analytes and DB516; delete-one-PSU jackknife with domain df = strata containing the domain; NCHS flags (n, n_eff < 30, KG width >= 0.30, df < 8).
alternatives_rejected: Unweighted analysis (describes the sample, not the population); WTMEC2YR for HbA1c (ignores blood-draw non-response); Taylor-only variance (no formula for kappa/AUC/standardised differences).

finding: Survey toolkit reproduces NCHS Data Brief 516 on the fasting subsample.
evidence_value: total 15.79% vs 15.8; diagnosed 11.30 vs 11.3; undiagnosed 4.49 vs 4.5; max |diff| 0.04 pp over 27 estimates
decision: Use src/survey.py (JK + KG + 3-band US 2000 standardisation) for every population number in S4-S9.
alternatives_rejected: Accept the toolkit on internal checks only (cannot detect wrong definitions or weights).

finding: US 2000 standard collapsed to 20-39/40-59/60+ = 0.3966/0.3718/0.2316, re-derived from the 5-year standard million.
decision: Direct age standardisation (3-band US 2000) for every between-group prevalence comparison; 6-band and internal standards as sensitivity.
alternatives_rejected: Crude comparisons (confounded by age); internal-only standard (not comparable with NCHS).
check_note: re-derived in-notebook; also validated indirectly by the DB516 age-adjusted replication

finding: NH Asian vs NH White L_comb: crude -0.8 pp (-5.1, 3.5) -> standardised +2.1 pp (-2.6, 6.8); README 18.0% vs 13.6% not reproducible.
decision: Withdraw the README 18.0/13.6 claim; report the Asian-White contrast only as an example of honest uncertainty (both CIs include 0).
alternatives_rejected: Headline 'Asians have higher diabetes prevalence' (not supported by the CI).
check_note: README figure corrected; numbers re-computed with three standards

finding: Insured - uninsured L_comb: crude +5.3 pp (1.8, 8.8) -> age-standardised +0.7 pp (-2.6, 3.9).
evidence_value: crude +5.3 (1.8, 8.8); std +0.7 (-2.6, 3.9); uninsured 60+ share 10.0% vs insured 33.7%
decision: Describe as age confounding (Age -> Medicare -> Insurance; Age -> diabetes) causing attenuation; never call it a reversal or Simpson's paradox.
alternatives_rejected: 'Insurance reversal' wording of the first draft (sign does not flip).

finding: Simpson scan: 224 comparisons, 6 sign flips, 10 attenuations > 50%; 4 flips come from mediator stratifiers (BMI, education).
evidence_value: uninsured x L_A1c | age -2.8 -> +1.1 pp, P(sign differs) = 0.72; Asian x L_comb | age P(sign differs) = 0.56 (B = 100)
decision: Treat the scan as exploratory; promote only DAG-supported (confounder-stratified) flips with CIs; never read BMI-stratified 'flips' as de-confounding (BMI is a mediator / mismeasured proxy of adiposity).
alternatives_rejected: Reporting all flips as findings (multiple comparisons, mediator conditioning); hiding the scan.
check_note: process doc quotes 219 comparisons / 5 flips; the pre-declared grid here gives 224 (= 252 - 28 self-stratifications)
